Reference: Xinge Yang, Qiang Fu and Wolfgang Heidrich,
"Curriculum learning for ab initio deep learned refractive optics,"
Nature Communications, 2024.

Adaptation by Optical System Design contributors, 2026-10-19:
Native C# cosine half-to-full aperture curriculum with full fields and all
configured wavelengths, bounded finite-difference Adam, and existing Core
trust-region polishing and independent dense validation. The upstream code
uses 0.5 times the aperture radius despite its prose saying 25 percent.

The separately identified autolens-managed-v1 path adds Core-owned forward
automatic tangents along formal intersections/refraction, implicit stop aiming,
two-phase Adam with explicit moments and cosine warm restarts, deterministic
area-stratified pupil resampling, normalized n/V catalog projection, and tied
spherical/even-aspheric cemented groups. The optimizable Cauchy reference uses
the upstream 0.587/0.486/0.656 micrometer wavelengths. The existing product's
manufacturing bounds, budgets and independent full-aperture acceptance remain
authoritative. This adaptation changes loss scaling, parameter normalization,
sampling, initialization and physical-domain handling for product integration.
The optional product target-polish handoff uses existing Core-backed native
numeric-Jacobian residual solvers, separately counted from the automatic-tangent
Adam stages. Non-descent Adam momentum restarts retain phase progress and use
an independent bias-correction age. Every accepted Adam step measures a decrease.

The historical paths are pure C#. They include no Python, PyTorch, DeepLens
runtime code or pretrained model weights. The historical CPU experiment
remains distinct and does not acquire the managed path's differentiation.
All optical computation uses the existing shared Optical System Design Core.
The original 2026-10-19 integration copied no upstream glass catalogs or prescriptions.
No upstream numerical equivalence or endorsement is claimed.

2026-10-24 reference-rule adaptation:
New desktop runs explicitly use autolens-upstream-e58-v2. The e58 default mobile
optimizer's initialization, fixed finite-object ray inputs, detached RGB losses,
linear constraints, physical parameter rates, direct Adam, phase schedules,
catalog handoff/rounding and periodic geometry pruning are implemented in C#.
Optical calculations and CPU/CUDA execution remain in the shared product Core.
Core remains double precision; training RNG and numerical-domain behavior do
not claim bitwise PyTorch equivalence. The original camera configuration has
not been reproduced as a separate complete topology.

Selected real dispersion entries from upstream MISC.AGF, PLASTIC2022.AGF,
CDGM.AGF and SCHOTT.AGF and the 61-entry CDGM_GLASS matching table are now
redistributed in Materials/Data/autolens-e58-materials.json under the upstream
Apache-2.0 notice. It contains original-file SHA256 hashes and the pinned
commit; names are prefixed AutoLensE58 and do not overwrite existing catalogs.
This records upstream data provenance and does not assert manufacturer
certification. No upstream optimized lens prescription or weights are shipped.

Target-preset adaptation, 2026-10-22: the pinned README's Lens Design Examples
are offered as native specification presets, not copied optimized prescriptions.
Undisclosed geometry, materials, wavelengths, seed ids, quality gates and CPU
budgets are explicitly local choices. The README body F/2 full-frame target is
retained despite inconsistent F/3 animation alt text. Ultra targets do not claim
reproduction of the eight unpublished prescriptions. See the product guide
docs/AUTOLENS_OFFICIAL_EXAMPLES.md for the source and adaptation boundaries.
